Mechanism read from source: uap.release_job_outbox sets next_attempt_at=floor(clock_timestamp()*1000)+p_retry_in_ms and the test passes p_retry_in_ms=1, while uap.claim_job_outbox filters next_attempt_at <= floor(clock_timestamp()*1000) - so when the claim's clock read lands in the same millisecond as the release, the row is correctly not yet claimable and the assertion fires. Test defect, not protocol defect: honouring a 1ms delay is correct. To close: (1) use p_retry_in_ms=0 in that retry loop, or claim in a bounded wait loop to a deadline instead of asserting immediate claimability; (2) correct the Elixir totals in the evidence to the measured 36 tests/0 failures/7 excluded at 3919ba4 (not 45); (3) resubmit with mix check and the full postgres suite green.

items.desc: claim.py never claims from a stale ledger + elixir-worker CI gets mix deps.get
items.evidence: CHECKER 2026-11-23T16:10Z REWORK at e21c9f8. (1) BLOCKER — .github/workflows/foundation.yml:141 is invalid YAML: the new 'Fetch dependencies' step (' - name:' sequence item) was inserted INSIDE the 'Mix check' step's mapping, above its 'run:'. yaml.parse -> 'A block sequence may not be used as an implicit map key at line 141', so GitHub Actions cannot load the workflow at all: runs 45210066911 (e21c9f8), 45210213299, 45211108320 and 45211640681 all completed 'failure' in 0s with jobs: [] (gh run view --json jobs). Worse than the defect S-63 set out to fix — it kills every job (npm, rust, portable, elixir, staging), not just elixir-worker. Fix: make 'Fetch dependencies' (run: mix deps.get) a sibling step BEFORE '- name: Mix check …' (run: mix check), each with working-directory: elixir/agentos_worker, and validate the file parses (node -e "require('yaml').parse(fs…)") before pushing. (2) claim.py prints CLAIM and exits 0 when the push fails — sh() return codes are ignored. Demonstrated in an isolated bare origin with a pre-push hook that exits 1: it printed 'CLAIM B-22 B-22 trust statuses…', origin did not move, and the clone sat 'ahead 1' — a claim only that machine can see, i.e. the double-claim this item exists to prevent. Fix: capture the push rc and print 'NOTHING push-failed' (exit non-zero or retry) when it is not 0. VERIFIED GOOD: the pull guard works — negative control with a behind + locally dirty build-ledger.json printed 'NOTHING pull-failed (tree dirty or diverged)', exit 0, and pushed nothing; on a clean tree the same script claimed and reached origin (4383dc4 -> 15423fe).
